newsitem.title: USA: Judge cautions jury in case against Arizona governor.
newsitem.headline: Judge cautions jury in case against Arizona governor.

text.p: The federal judge presiding over the fraud trial of Arizona Gov. Fife Symington admonished the jury Wednesday about discussing the case after a reporter said he overheard two jurors talking about it on the courthouse steps.

Judge Roger Strand issued the warning after becoming aware of allegations that two jurors were overheard discussing Symington's taxes as they left U.S. District Court in Phoenix. His taxes were mentioned in court Tuesday.
"It is not anything the court intends to pursue," Strand told jurors, adding that the details of Tuesday's incident were sketchy.
Attorneys from both sides said they did not believe that the incident -- one of several that have occurred during the 12-week-trial -- was cause for a mistrial.

But it did prompt The Associated Press to temporarily pull its reporter who has been covering the trial of Symington, who faces 22 counts of fraud, attempted extortion and perjury and could be ousted from office.
Reporter Jerry Nachtigal was the person who witnessed the conversation and reported it later that day.
"We were concerned that he might be called as a witness about what he heard," said Sue Cross, the AP's bureau chief in Phoenix.
Cross said she wanted to discuss the matter with the wire service's attorneys before bringing the reporter back.
Meanwhile, Symington remained on the stand as prosecutors walk him through the documents that were compiled during his days as a developer in the mid-1980s to early 1990s.
He is the last witness for the defence. The jury is expected to get the case in mid-August.
